subject: ophthalmology
title: Congenital and secondary glaucoma

steps.tx: **Primary congenital glaucoma** (about 1 in 10,000 births, trabeculodysgenesis) enlarges the elastic infant eye (**buphthalmos**, ox eye) with tearing, photophobia, blepharospasm, hazy enlarged cornea (Haab striae from Descemet tears) and high pressure. Clouding that clears with pressure control differs from congenital hereditary endothelial dystrophy. Treatment is surgical: **goniotomy** or trabeculotomy opening the angle, with trabeculectomy or tubes for failures; drops only bridge to theatre under examination anaesthesia. Early surgery saves vision before amblyopia and optic damage fix.
steps.say: Tearing photophobic big hazy eye in infant is congenital glaucoma: operate the angle early.

steps.tx: **Steroid induced glaucoma** clogs trabeculum in responders (children, myopes, POAG families) within weeks of potent drops, so every steroid course needs scheduled pressure checks, switching to fluorometholone or ciclosporin where possible. **Uveitic glaucoma** mixes inflammatory debris, synechial closure and steroid response, needing inflammation control (aqueous suppressants, judicious laser, tubes over trabeculectomy in inflamed eyes). Herpetic trabeculitis spikes pressure with mild cells (Posner Schlossman pattern). Pigment dispersion (young myopic men, Krukenberg spindle, exercise induced storms) and pseudoexfoliation (white flakes, poor dilation, weak zonules complicating cataract surgery) are special open angle patterns.
steps.say: Steroid drops demand pressure checks. Flakes on lens with poor dilation is pseudoexfoliation: zonules are weak.

steps.tx: **Neovascular glaucoma** (100 day glaucoma after central retinal vein occlusion, proliferative diabetic retinopathy) grows fibrovascular membrane over angle causing intractable pain with high pressure and rubeosis; panretinal photocoagulation regresses drive while tubes or cyclodestruction palliate (trabeculectomy fails on bleeding membranes). Treat the ischaemia, not just the pressure. **Lens induced** emergencies: phacomorphic (swollen lens, extract urgently) and phacolytic (leaked protein, wash out with extraction). Malignant (aqueous misdirection) shallows centrally after surgery needing cycloplegics and vitrectomy patterns.
steps.say: Red painful blind eye with new vessels on iris after vein occlusion: neovascular, laser the retina.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Traumatic angle recession (hyphaema with gonioscopic cleft) glaucomas months later, so lifetime pressure surveillance follows blunt injury; ghost cell glaucoma (degenerate vitreous blood clogging meshwork) follows vitrectomy or trauma. Iridocorneal endothelial syndromes, Axenfeld Rieger and aniridia (with foveal hypoplasia and nystagmus) are developmental angle glaucomas needing lifelong follow up. Surgical choice respects cause: goniotomy for congenital, tubes for inflamed or scarred conjunctiva, cyclodestruction for blind painful eyes.
steps.say: Blunt eye injury needs pressure checks for life. Blind painful glaucomatous eye gets cyclodestruction.
